destinations.name: San Francisco
destinations.summary: Hills, fog, and a real comeback: 24.2 million visitors forecast for 2026, a 14 percent hotel tax, 9 dollar cable cars, and Alcatraz tickets that sell out weeks ahead.
destinations.headline: San Francisco in 2026: The Views Never Left, the Hotel Bill Is Bigger Than It Looks
destinations.body:
San Francisco is busy again. Visitor numbers have climbed back past where they were before 2020, and the things people come for never moved: the Golden Gate, the grid of absurd hills, Golden Gate Park, the cable cars, and the food in the Mission, Chinatown and the Richmond.

The city is easy to love and easy to overpay for. The room rate on a booking site is not the bill. San Francisco charges a 14 percent transient occupancy tax on stays of under 30 days, and many hotels add a Tourism Improvement District assessment of 2 to 2.25 percent as a separate line. On a 300 dollar night that is roughly 48 dollars before parking, which downtown hotels charge for separately and heavily.

Alcatraz is the ticket people get wrong. It is a National Park Service site reached only on Alcatraz City Cruises from Pier 33, and the adult day tour is 47.95 dollars. Night tours are 59.65 dollars and go first. In summer and October, dates can be gone weeks out. Anything sold as an Alcatraz tour by somebody else needs a close read, because some of them sail past the island instead of landing on it.

The cable cars are a real 19th century machine and worth riding once. A single ride is 9 dollars with no transfer. For everything else, Muni is 2.85 dollars on Clipper or a contactless card and covers 120 minutes. Fog is the weather, not a forecast: July can be cold at the beach and September and October are usually the warmest weeks of the year. Phone and car break ins are the practical crime risk; leave nothing visible in a parked car, anywhere.
destinations.what_great: The setting is the point and it is free: walking up Russian Hill, across the Golden Gate Bridge or through Golden Gate Park costs nothing. The food is excellent at every price, from Mission burritos to dim sum in the Richmond. Muni and BART make a car unnecessary inside the city, and the cable cars and Alcatraz are rare things that live up to the postcard.
destinations.what_ruined: It is expensive, and the hotel bill grows by about 16 percent after the posted rate once the occupancy tax and district assessment land. Alcatraz sells out and copycat tours muddy the booking. Car break ins and phone snatching are common enough that locals plan around them. Summer visitors pack for California and meet fog and wind instead.

rating_rationale.overall: A world class setting with excellent food and transit, held back by price and street level petty crime.
rating_rationale.safety: Violent crime against visitors is uncommon, but car break ins and phone theft are frequent and well documented.
rating_rationale.value: Hotel rates plus a 14 percent occupancy tax and a district assessment make it one of the costlier city stays in the United States.

tips: Book Alcatraz only with Alcatraz City Cruises, the one ferry the National Park Service authorizes. The adult day tour is 47.95 dollars and leaves from Pier 33.
Budget for 14 percent transient occupancy tax on stays under 30 days, plus a 2 to 2.25 percent Tourism Improvement District line at many hotels.
A cable car ride is 9 dollars with no transfer. Ride the Powell and Hyde line once for the view down to the bay, then use Muni at 2.85 dollars on Clipper or a contactless card.
Never leave a bag, a charger or anything else visible in a parked car, including at viewpoints like Twin Peaks and the Palace of Fine Arts.
Pack a warm layer in July and August. September and October are usually the warmest and clearest weeks.

guide.title: San Francisco Travel Guide 2026: Alcatraz, Cable Cars, Hotel Tax and When to Go
guide.summary: Getting around without a car, what Alcatraz and the cable cars cost in 2026, what the hotel tax adds, and when the fog lifts.
guide.body:
Most visitors fly into San Francisco International (SFO). BART runs from the airport into downtown, so a car is optional and usually a cost rather than a help: downtown hotel parking is charged separately and break ins are the most common crime against visitors.

Inside the city, Muni buses, streetcars and light rail cost 2.85 dollars on Clipper, MuniMobile or a contactless card, and the fare covers 120 minutes. The cable cars are separate at 9 dollars a single ride with no transfer. Pay cash with exact change, Clipper or MuniMobile.

Alcatraz is the one booking to make as soon as dates are firm. Alcatraz City Cruises is the only ferry the National Park Service authorizes, it leaves from Pier 33, and the adult day tour is 47.95 dollars including the ferry and audio tour. Night tours are 59.65 dollars.

For museums, the California Academy of Sciences in Golden Gate Park lists adult tickets at 49 dollars and 55 dollars on peak dates, so pick the date in the booking flow before budgeting.

When to go: September and October are usually the warmest, clearest weeks. June to August is often foggy and cool near the ocean. Hotels cost more during big conventions, so check rates across a few dates before committing.

Where to walk: Russian Hill and the Hyde Street cable car line, North Beach, Chinatown, the Mission, Golden Gate Park and the bridge itself. Fisherman's Wharf is where the Alcatraz ferry leaves, not the best part of the city.

facts_checked.fact: Alcatraz adult day tour 47.95 dollars, night tour 59.65 dollars; Alcatraz City Cruises is the only NPS authorized ferry
Cable car single ride 9 dollars; Muni adult single 2.85 dollars on Clipper, MuniMobile or card, good for 120 minutes
14 percent transient occupancy tax on stays under 30 days
California Academy of Sciences adult 49 dollars, 55 dollars on peak dates

destinations.name: Manaus
destinations.summary: A gilded opera house in the Amazon, the Meeting of the Waters, and the real jungle a boat ride away, with yellow fever prep and app-only transport as the price of entry.
destinations.headline: Manaus in 2026: A 20 Reais Opera House, the Meeting of the Waters, and a Jungle You Must Book Properly
destinations.body:
Manaus is a working city of about two million people in the middle of the Amazon, and most visitors use it as the door to the rainforest. It deserves a day or two of its own.

Teatro Amazonas is the reason. The opera house was built in the rubber boom and is still a working theatre, and a guided visit costs 20 reais in 2026, with a 10 reais half rate for students, teachers and visitors aged 60 and over. Visits run Tuesday to Saturday from 9am to 5pm and only 9am to 1pm on Sundays and holidays, which catches people who come back from a river trip on a Sunday afternoon.

The Meeting of the Waters is the other sight that lives up to the description: the dark Rio Negro and the pale Solimoes run side by side for kilometres before they mix. Day boats from the city do the trip routinely.

The jungle itself is where trips go well or badly. A lodge stay with a licensed guide, booked before you land, costs real money because it includes boats, fuel and food far from a road. The cheap version is an offer in the arrivals hall or on a WhatsApp message from somebody with no company behind them. Walk past the touts at Eduardo Gomes airport and use Uber, 99 or the official taxi desk.

Health preparation is not optional here. The US CDC recommends yellow fever vaccination for travelers going to Amazonas state and lists all of Amazonas as a malaria area. See a travel clinic weeks before you go, not the week of the flight.
destinations.what_great: The opera house is genuinely astonishing and costs 20 reais to see properly. The Meeting of the Waters is a real natural spectacle a short boat ride from the port. A well run lodge puts you in primary rainforest with guides who know it, which is the reason most people make the trip.
destinations.what_ruined: Cheap jungle offers with no company behind them are the main way trips go wrong. Health preparation takes planning: yellow fever vaccination is recommended for the state and malaria is present. The city is hot, humid and spread out, so you rely on ride apps, and the Sunday hours at the opera house trip people up.

rating_rationale.overall: A unique combination of a historic opera house and direct access to the Amazon, provided the jungle part is booked with a licensed operator.
rating_rationale.safety: Petty theft and phone snatching are the practical city risks, and health risks from yellow fever and malaria need preparation.
rating_rationale.value: City sights are cheap, with the opera house at 20 reais; lodge trips cost more but include transport and guiding that cannot be done cheaply safely.

tips: A guided visit to Teatro Amazonas is 20 reais, or 10 reais at the half rate. It is open Tuesday to Saturday 9am to 5pm, and only 9am to 1pm on Sundays and holidays.
See a travel clinic early: the US CDC recommends yellow fever vaccination for Amazonas state and lists the whole state as a malaria area.
Book a jungle lodge with a registered operator before you land, and ignore guides who approach you in the airport arrivals hall.
Use Uber, 99 or the official airport taxi desk, and use ride apps door to door after dark.
US, Canadian and Australian citizens have needed a Brazilian e-visa since April 2025. Check the current rule for your passport before you book.

guide.title: Manaus Travel Guide 2026: Teatro Amazonas, the Meeting of the Waters and Booking the Jungle
guide.summary: What the opera house costs and when it opens, how to see the Meeting of the Waters, how to book a lodge safely, and the health preparation the Amazon needs.
guide.body:
Manaus is reached by air through Eduardo Gomes International Airport (MAO). The airport is fine; the arrivals hall is where unlicensed taxis and informal guides wait. Use Uber, 99 or the official taxi desk, and have your lodge transfer arranged in writing before you fly.

Day one in the city: Teatro Amazonas. Guided visits cost 20 reais, half rate 10 reais for students, teachers and visitors 60 and over on proof, and free for children up to 10. Hours are Tuesday to Saturday 9am to 5pm, and Sundays and holidays 9am to 1pm only. The square in front of it, Largo de Sao Sebastiao, is the pleasant part of the old centre for an evening.

Day two: the Meeting of the Waters, where the black Rio Negro and the sandy Solimoes run side by side before mixing. Day boat trips from the city port cover it, often combined with a stop in the flooded forest.

The jungle: two or three nights at a lodge is the usual trip. Choose an operator with a website, a registered company and written prices that include transfers, meals and guiding. Last minute offers from people without those are where things go wrong.

Health: the US CDC recommends yellow fever vaccination for travelers to Amazonas state and lists the state as a malaria area, so talk to a travel clinic about both several weeks ahead. Bring repellent and long sleeves for dawn and dusk.

Entry: US, Canadian and Australian citizens have needed a Brazilian e-visa since April 10, 2025. Check the rule for your passport with Brazil's official channels before booking.

facts_checked.fact: Teatro Amazonas guided visit 20 reais, half 10 reais; Tuesday to Saturday 9am to 5pm, Sundays and holidays 9am to 1pm
CDC recommends yellow fever vaccine for travelers to Amazonas state; all of Amazonas is a malaria transmission area
Brazil visa requirement for nationals of Australia, Canada and the United States took effect April 10, 2025

destinations.name: Buzios
destinations.summary: Twenty-three beaches on a peninsula three hours from Rio, still the easy Brazilian beach town Brigitte Bardot put on the map, reachable by bus from about 19 US dollars.
destinations.headline: Buzios in 2026: Many Beaches, One Bus From Rio, and Summer Prices to Plan Around
destinations.body:
Armacao dos Buzios is a small peninsula town about 170 kilometres east of Rio de Janeiro, and it is still the easiest beach escape from the city. Brigitte Bardot's visit in 1964 made it famous; the beaches are what keep it busy.

The peninsula has a long list of beaches within a short ride of each other, and they are different enough to choose by mood. Geriba is the long surf beach. Azeda and Azedinha are small, calm coves near the centre. Joao Fernandes is the busy, pretty one with restaurants on the sand. In the evening everyone walks Rua das Pedras and the Orla Bardot waterfront.

Getting there is simple. Fly into Rio, then take an Auto Viacao 1001 coach from Rodoviaria Novo Rio. The scheduled run is about three and a half hours, more when the traffic out of Rio is bad, and tickets are sold on the operator's site and app, so check the current fare there rather than trusting an old number. Driving takes about three hours on a good day.

Timing matters more than in Rio. January to March is the Brazilian summer holiday: hot, wetter, crowded and at its most expensive. The southern winter, roughly June to September, is drier and milder, and the shoulder months are the quiet, cheaper option. Once there, you can walk much of the town, and local vans along the main avenue are the cheap way between beaches.
destinations.what_great: Many very different beaches packed onto one small peninsula, most of them a short ride apart. An easy, direct coach connection from Rio. A compact, walkable town centre with a good evening scene on Rua das Pedras and the waterfront.
destinations.what_ruined: Brazilian summer, January to March, brings crowds, rain and peak prices. The best known beaches, Joao Fernandes in particular, fill up fast. Prices in the centre are high for Brazil, and the coach from Rio can stretch well past three and a half hours in heavy traffic.

rating_rationale.overall: A relaxed, beautiful beach town with real variety, easy to reach from Rio.
rating_rationale.safety: Calmer than Rio; the usual beach town petty theft is the main concern.
rating_rationale.value: Getting there is cheap by coach, but central restaurants and summer accommodation are priced well above the Brazilian average.

tips: Take the Auto Viacao 1001 coach from Rodoviaria Novo Rio. Plan on about three and a half hours and check the current fare in the operator's app or site.
Pick a beach by what you want: Geriba for surf, Azeda and Azedinha for calm water, Joao Fernandes for restaurants on the sand.
Avoid January to March unless you want the Brazilian summer crowd and peak prices; June to September is drier and milder.
Walk Rua das Pedras and the Orla Bardot in the evening, and use the local vans on the main avenue to hop between beaches.
US, Canadian and Australian citizens have needed a Brazilian e-visa since April 2025. Check the current rule for your passport before you book.

guide.title: Buzios Travel Guide 2026: Getting There From Rio, Which Beach, and When to Go
guide.summary: How to get from Rio to Buzios by coach, which beaches suit which trip, and why the season changes the price more than anything else.
guide.body:
Buzios, officially Armacao dos Buzios, sits on a peninsula in Rio de Janeiro state about 170 kilometres east of the city of Rio. Most visitors fly into Rio (GIG or SDU) and continue overland.

By coach: Auto Viacao 1001 runs direct services from Rodoviaria Novo Rio. The scheduled journey is about three and a half hours and can be longer when traffic leaving Rio is heavy. Buy on the operator's site or app, where the current fare and departure times are listed. By car the trip is about three hours in good traffic.

Which beach: Geriba is long and open with surf. Ferradura is a sheltered horseshoe bay. Azeda and Azedinha are small coves close to the centre, reached on foot. Joao Fernandes is the lively one, with restaurants and loungers on the sand. Schooner trips from the town pier visit several beaches in an afternoon.

Where to stay: the centre around Rua das Pedras suits people who want to walk to dinner; Geriba and Ferradura suit people who want the beach on the doorstep.

When to go: January to March is high summer and Brazilian holiday season, hot and wet with the highest prices. June to September is the drier, milder southern winter. April, May, October and November are the quieter shoulder months.

Pair it with Rio: a few days in the city and a few at the beach is the classic combination, and the coach makes it a single easy transfer.

facts_checked.fact: Auto Viacao 1001 operates direct coaches from Rodoviaria Novo Rio to Armacao dos Buzios, scheduled about 3 hours 30 minutes
Brazil visa requirement for nationals of Australia, Canada and the United States took effect April 10, 2025
